I want the research problem, overall approach, main findings, and limitations in one readable summary, not citation-ready notes and not a method-only audit: We study whether explicit task decomposition improves the reliability of tool-using language agents on long-horizon tasks. Our system first predicts a structured plan, then retrieves candidate tools for each subtask, and finally executes the plan step by step with intermediate state tracking. We evaluate on a benchmark of multi-step personal-assistant tasks and compare against direct prompting and lightweight replanning baselines. The decomposed system improves task completion and reduces cascading errors, especially on longer tasks. However, most gains appear on structured benchmarks with known tool interfaces, and we do not establish that the same advantage transfers to noisier real-world environments.
